en.description: Reprompt Video to Prompt turns video references into AI prompts. See supported inputs, pricing, limitations and official sources before choosing a video-to-prompt tool.
en.lead: Four frames. One reusable video prompt.
en.sublead: The browser samples a short clip. Only the still frames are sent for analysis, according to Reprompt; no account is needed.

steps.title: Trim to one shot.
steps.text: The site recommends a short clip of roughly 3–20 seconds.

steps.title: Review the four frames.
steps.text: If playback fails, use two to four screenshots instead.

steps.title: Add context and copy.
steps.text: Choose a model; add motion or sound details the stills cannot show.

good: You want to start without an account.
You prefer sending selected frames rather than the full video file.
consider: You need precise timing across many cuts.
You expect four images to capture every motion or sound.

faq.a: It is free without an account or card, but daily and pace limits apply. The tool page does not publish a fixed daily number.

faq.q: Does the whole video leave my device?
faq.a: The tool page says only four JPEG frames are sent; the video remains on your device. This is the service’s statement, not a network audit by ToolFavor.

faq.q: How long should the clip be?
faq.a: The site recommends one shot of roughly 3–20 seconds. Several cuts can mix unrelated scenes into the four frames.

faq.q: What if MOV does not open?
faq.a: Compatibility depends on browser playback. Try a compatible MP4/WebM or use two to four screenshots.

faq.q: Does it generate a finished video?
faq.a: No. This tool writes a prompt; paste it into a separate video model. It cannot guarantee the original creator’s wording.
